tier_reason: Lowered B to C on the enricher's provenance and equivalence findings (DASP precedent): the libvips wiki row is dated 12 Aug 2025 but vips-bench's ffmpeg.sh was first committed 2025-09-21, and until commit c4dbb24 (2026-04-12) benchmark.sh passed '-o' as its second argument, which ffmpeg 7.1 rejects ('Unrecognized option'), so the committed driver could not have produced the 2.06 s row and the row was not re-run after the fix. The compared work also differs: FFmpeg's convolution filter is planar-only and tiffenc lacks GBRP, so the pipeline converts to limited-range YUV444P, sharpens Y, Cb and Cr and writes a PackBits YCbCr TIFF, not the RGB output ImageMagick produces. The independent measurement exists but is not reproducible from the public scripts, so first-party-grade evidence at most.

corrections.caveats: The 2.06 s row is not reproducible from the committed vips-bench scripts: ffmpeg.sh postdates the wiki date (first commit 2025-09-21) and benchmark.sh passed an '-o' option that ffmpeg 7.1 rejects until 2026-04-12, with no re-run afterwards. Output is not equivalent to ImageMagick's: FFmpeg converts to limited-range YUV444P, sharpens the Y, Cb and Cr planes and writes a PackBits YCbCr TIFF. One trivial I/O-dominated test (the wiki says it flatters libvips), so the ratio mostly reflects TIFF reading and writing and pipeline overhead rather than libswscale; ffmpeg reads the strip TIFF and resamples with libswscale's default bicubic while ImageMagick reads the tiled TIFF with crop-on-load and -filter triangle.
